name: HONG KONG

flag.title: Hong Kong Flag
flag.note: Red with a white bauhinia flower

lead: Hong Kong is a small city on China's coast. Skyscrapers climb steep hills right to the harbour. Britain ruled it until 1997. Now it is part of China, but it keeps its own laws and money. About seven million people live here.
geo: Hong Kong spreads across a peninsula and 263 islands. The harbour between Hong Kong Island and Kowloon is so deep that giant cargo ships park in the city.
More than 70% of the land is countryside, with jungle hills and beaches. Yet Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city on Earth.
animals: Shy Chinese pangolins roll into a scaly ball when scared. They shuffle through the forest at night. Wild boars trot through suburbs.
The Mai Po wetlands see more than 400 kinds of birds, including the rare black-faced spoonbill. Green turtles nest on quiet beaches.
culture: Families meet for yum cha. Bamboo steamers of har gow and siu mai roll to the table. Every autumn, the Hungry Ghost Festival fills streets with burning paper gifts.
Neon signs, lucky red envelopes and firecrackers mark the Cantonese calendar. People watch horse races at Happy Valley, a track inside the city since 1846.
history: Fishers lived here for thousands of years. Britain took Hong Kong Island in 1842, after the First Opium War. The place grew into a big trading port.
On 1 July 1997 Hong Kong rejoined China under 'one country, two systems'. It keeps its own courts and currency until at least 2047.
wows: Hong Kong has more Rolls-Royce cars per person than anywhere else.
The MTR metro runs on time for 99.9% of journeys.
Land reclamation has added about 70 km² of new ground.
The world's longest outdoor covered escalator is 800 m long.
Over 90% of daily trips use public transport.
The Peak Tram has climbed the same hill since 1888.
Hong Kong has over 1,000 buildings taller than 100 m.

myths.myth: Fortune cookies are a Chinese food
myths.fact: They became popular in California about 100 years ago. They are not a traditional Chinese sweet.

myths.myth: Bamboo is too weak to build with
myths.fact: Bamboo is light but very strong. Builders in Hong Kong still use bamboo scaffolds on skyscrapers.
